## Specific checks

The historical await is non-Clone and constructed from actual query/selected
row/update data. It stays outside Clone/Eq Core and carries a fresh playback
scope, original position, original Post pin and exact source-derived mutations.
Prepared→PostVerified requires matching scope/position, independently expected
raw TLNM comparison, and actual historical full-KV plus directory equality.
PostVerified does not release the source await. Its separate Resolve requires
that same active position/Post and can produce one evaluation; duplicate or
foreign calls refuse. Rejected source updates/no-match do not consume a native
transition. The public metadata helper is not a financial verdict constructor.

The shared row PC body retains Prefix/PrimaryValidity/FatalMark/FatalValidity/
Done/Stopped and the same real Runtime/queue. The old live preparer still does
query first, returns completed/no-match before the update hook, then runs the
actual update failure hook and original opaque preparation. Historical mode
uses the same PC and actual computed parameters. On raw append mismatch the
row records a sticky storage stop; another Advance cannot decode/mark/reenter
source. After verified Post, only the actual validity-result transition clears
the held plan and advances that same PC. No bridge method takes financial
effects. Existing completed-row replay still compares complete receipts, source
state and original physical bindings before returning an accepted Session.

I extracted the actual old fdfa8ea context formatter and TLNM encoder. Both
factorings are equal after their documented parameter-name substitutions;
normalization removed whitespace ONLY outside string/byte-string literals.
BODY_EQUIVALENCE.json and the captured old sources preserve this check. The
legacy synchronous cleanup only clears its own unexposed Prepared reservation;
the additional retained-await control verifies it cannot clear an active
externally held await.

Cold guards cover put/native DB/import, discard including context-only updates,
prepared commits, compaction/configuration, and the additional escrow retain/
guarded-commit APIs before their I/O. Scope rejection does not consume a live
append token. Foreign/nested/stale capabilities cannot release another owner.
Metadata constructors create a distinct scoped owner and still require the real
exclusive lock; they are not an escape from a retained rejected financial owner.
